title: Two Ways Out: Blood and Wires

scenes.tts: The hypothalamus has a correction to send. How does it leave the brain, and how fast?
scenes.visual: Sagittal sketch of the hypothalamus with the pituitary below. The question appears above.
scenes.narration: The hypothalamus has a correction to send. How does it leave the brain, and how fast?

scenes.tts: Nerves often act within seconds. Hormone effects usually build more slowly, over minutes to hours.
scenes.visual: Two exits light up: a nerve (often seconds) and a blood vessel (usually minutes, for vasopressin, to hours, for cortisol and thyroid hormone).
scenes.narration: Nerves often act within seconds. Hormone effects usually build more slowly, over minutes to hours.

scenes.tts: Start with vasopressin. Large neurons in the supraoptic and paraventricular nuclei make it. Their axons release it in the posterior pituitary, straight into the blood.
scenes.visual: Magnocellular neurons glow in two nuclei (labels: SON, PVN); their axons run down the stalk into the posterior lobe, and dots of vasopressin leave the terminals into a vessel.
scenes.narration: Start with vasopressin. Large neurons in the supraoptic and paraventricular nuclei make it. Their axons release it in the posterior pituitary, straight into the blood.

scenes.tts: So the posterior lobe stores and releases vasopressin. It does not make it.
scenes.visual: Label on the posterior lobe: stores and releases, does not make.
scenes.narration: So the posterior lobe stores and releases vasopressin. It does not make it.

scenes.tts: The anterior lobe is reached by blood instead. Neurons release peptides into capillaries at the median eminence.
scenes.visual: Neurons end at the base of the hypothalamus; peptide dots enter a capillary bed. Label: median eminence.
scenes.narration: The anterior lobe is reached by blood instead. Neurons release peptides into capillaries at the median eminence.

scenes.tts: Portal veins carry them down the stalk to a second capillary bed. They arrive concentrated, before the general circulation dilutes them.
scenes.visual: Dots travel down portal veins in the stalk into a second capillary bed in the anterior lobe. Label: portal system, two capillary beds in series.
scenes.narration: Portal veins carry them down the stalk to a second capillary bed. They arrive concentrated, before the general circulation dilutes them.

scenes.tts: Take the stress axis. The paraventricular nucleus releases corticotropin-releasing hormone, C R H. That drives adrenocorticotropic hormone, A C T H, from the pituitary.
scenes.caption: Take the stress axis. The paraventricular nucleus releases corticotropin-releasing hormone, CRH. That drives adrenocorticotropic hormone, ACTH, from the pituitary.
scenes.visual: The HPA axis builds: PVN, CRH, anterior pituitary, ACTH.
scenes.narration: Take the stress axis. The paraventricular nucleus releases corticotropin-releasing hormone, CRH. That drives adrenocorticotropic hormone, ACTH, from the pituitary.

scenes.tts: A C T H drives cortisol from the adrenal cortex. Cortisol feeds back on the hypothalamus and pituitary, and turns the axis down.
scenes.caption: ACTH drives cortisol from the adrenal cortex. Cortisol feeds back on the hypothalamus and pituitary, and turns the axis down.
scenes.visual: ACTH arrow to the adrenal cortex; cortisol arrow loops back with minus signs at the hypothalamus and pituitary.
scenes.narration: ACTH drives cortisol from the adrenal cortex. Cortisol feeds back on the hypothalamus and pituitary, and turns the axis down.

scenes.tts: Same loop, different variable: here, a hormone.
scenes.visual: Label beside the axis: same loop, the regulated variable is cortisol. A smaller thyroid axis appears beside it with the same shape.
scenes.narration: Same loop, different variable: here, a hormone.

scenes.tts: Now the wires. The usual autonomic chain has two neurons and two synapses: one in a ganglion, one on the target.
scenes.visual: A two-neuron chain from the spinal cord to an organ. The ganglion synapse and the target synapse are circled. Small note: usual route; one exception later.
scenes.narration: Now the wires. The usual autonomic chain has two neurons and two synapses: one in a ganglion, one on the target.

scenes.tts: Rule one. The first synapse is the same everywhere: acetylcholine, acting mainly on nicotinic receptors.
scenes.visual: Four chains appear side by side. Every preganglionic axon is blue. Label: rule 1, ACh to nicotinic, in every ganglion.
scenes.narration: Rule one. The first synapse is the same everywhere: acetylcholine, acting mainly on nicotinic receptors.

scenes.tts: Rule two. The second synapse usually names the division. Parasympathetic: acetylcholine on muscarinic receptors. Most sympathetic: noradrenaline on adrenergic receptors.
scenes.visual: The parasympathetic postganglionic axon turns blue (ACh to muscarinic); the main sympathetic postganglionic axon turns red (noradrenaline to alpha, beta).
scenes.narration: Rule two. The second synapse usually names the division. Parasympathetic: acetylcholine on muscarinic receptors. Most sympathetic: noradrenaline on adrenergic receptors.

scenes.tts: Atropine blocks muscarinic receptors. Give a large dose. What happens to the heart rate? And to sweating?
scenes.visual: A large atropine label blocks the muscarinic receptors on a heart and a sweat gland. Question marks on each.
scenes.narration: Atropine blocks muscarinic receptors. Give a large dose. What happens to the heart rate? And to sweating?

scenes.tts: At a large dose, the heart rate rises. The vagal brake on the heart's own pacemaker was on all the time, even at rest.
scenes.visual: A heart-rate trace climbs. A brake icon on the vagus nerve, pressing on the pacemaker, is removed.
scenes.narration: At a large dose, the heart rate rises. The vagal brake on the heart's own pacemaker was on all the time, even at rest.

scenes.tts: Sweating stops. The sympathetic fibres to sweat glands release acetylcholine onto muscarinic receptors. That is the first exception.
scenes.visual: The sweat-gland chain is highlighted: short blue, chain ganglion, long blue. Label: exception 1.
scenes.narration: Sweating stops. The sympathetic fibres to sweat glands release acetylcholine onto muscarinic receptors. That is the first exception.

scenes.tts: Separate tests show steady sympathetic drive too. So the heart sits at a balance, like a sink filled from two taps.
scenes.visual: A sink with a cold tap (parasympathetic) and a hot tap (sympathetic). Turning either changes the temperature. At rest the cold tap runs stronger. Small label: analogy only.
scenes.narration: Separate tests show steady sympathetic drive too. So the heart sits at a balance, like a sink filled from two taps.

scenes.tts: The second exception is the adrenal medulla. There, the second neuron has become a gland that releases adrenaline and noradrenaline into the blood.
scenes.visual: The adrenal chain: a blue preganglionic axon ends on a chromaffin cell that releases adrenaline into a vessel. Label: exception 2.
scenes.narration: The second exception is the adrenal medulla. There, the second neuron has become a gland that releases adrenaline and noradrenaline into the blood.

scenes.tts: The paraventricular nucleus uses every route: portal blood, the posterior lobe, and descending autonomic pathways.
scenes.visual: The PVN lights up with three outputs at once: to portal blood, to the posterior lobe, and down toward the brainstem and spinal cord.
scenes.narration: The paraventricular nucleus uses every route: portal blood, the posterior lobe, and descending autonomic pathways.

scenes.tts: Two routes out. Nerves often work in seconds. Hormone effects usually build over minutes to hours.
scenes.visual: Takeaway card: wires, often seconds; blood, usually minutes to hours. Two rules and two exceptions cover the main autonomic synapses.
scenes.narration: Two routes out. Nerves often work in seconds. Hormone effects usually build over minutes to hours.
